response: No, motion perception deficit in schizophrenia is not solely a consequence of eye-tracking abnormality. While individuals with schizophrenia often exhibit eye-tracking abnormalities, research suggests that motion perception deficits are a separate cognitive impairment that can occur independently of eye movement issues. Studies have shown that people with schizophrenia may have difficulty perceiving motion even when their eye movements are normal, indicating a more complex underlying neural mechanism contributing to this deficit.
